battle.name: 第三次塞米諾爾戰爭
battle.theater: 佛州西南大柏樹沼澤與威拉庫奇河
battle.brief: 一八五五年起，佛州當局以增兵、禁運與保留地制度逼最後一批塞米諾爾人西遷，同年十二月邁爾斯堡外的馬車隊伏擊拉開第三次塞米諾爾戰爭。此後三年，雙方在威拉庫奇河、大柏樹沼澤與奧基喬比湖反覆拉鋸：聯軍以雷管步槍在雨霧中遠距精射，卻屢遭游擊與後勤襲擊牽制，最後以金錢買下西遷。

kit.name: 雷管步槍
kit.history: 雷管取代火燧之後，底火在霧裡也打得響。射程變長，隊形就散了。

countries: 交戰的一方是美利堅合眾國聯邦政府與佛羅里達州政府，另一方是拒絕遷出佛州的塞米諾爾各部族。聯邦方面由陸軍部統籌，戰區內常駐第四砲兵團與第五步兵團，另有海軍與陸戰隊沿海岸巡邏；一八五六年起，州民兵有十個連被聯邦政府收編，而聯邦兵力在一八五五年底已超過七百人駐於佛州半島。州政府方面，佛羅里達州長詹姆斯·布魯姆在邁爾斯堡遭襲之後組織志願連隊，其中兩個步兵連與三個騎兵連約二百六十人獲國防部長傑佛遜·戴維斯接納，另有約四百人留在州政府直接指揮之下；這些州部隊的裝備多靠民間捐款購置，槍械口徑混雜。州方另任命傑西·卡特將軍為「無軍階特別代理」統率州部隊。聯邦方面先後由准將威廉·哈尼接管戰區，哈尼調離後由上校古斯塔夫斯·盧米斯接任。塞米諾爾一方沒有常設指揮部，由比利·鮑萊格斯、薩姆·瓊斯、奇普科、奧斯森·圖斯滕吉等各部族首領分頭行動，另有尤奇、喬克托等族群的殘餘成員隨隊作戰。
countriesEn: The two sides were the government of the United States, federal and state, and the Seminole bands who refused to leave Florida. On the federal side the War Department in Washington ran the campaign, with the 4th Artillery and the 5th Infantry stationed in the theatre and Navy and Marine patrols working the coast; from 1856 ten companies of Florida militia were taken into federal service, and the federal presence on the Florida peninsula topped seven hundred men by the end of 1855. The state side was organised by Governor James Broome after the raid on Hartsuff's camp: two infantry companies and three mounted companies, about two hundred and sixty men in all, were accepted by Secretary of War Jefferson Davis, while another four hundred men stayed under state control; much of that equipment was bought with private donations, so the calibres were mixed. Broome also appointed General Jesse Carter as a 'special agent without military rank' to lead the state troops. On the federal side Brigadier General William S. Harney took over the theatre, and after Harney was transferred away Colonel Gustavus Loomis succeeded him. The Seminole side had no permanent headquarters: Billy Bowlegs, Sam Jones, Chipco, Oscen Tustenuggee and other band leaders acted on their own authority, and small groups of Yuchi and Choctaw origin still fought alongside them.
people: 塞米諾爾方面，比利·鮑萊格斯是第三次塞米諾爾戰爭最具代表性的首領。一八五二年他被遷徙使盧瑟·布萊克帶往華盛頓，總統米勒德·費爾莫爾頒給他一枚銀章，他與另外三名首領簽下遷徙協議，回程後即全部推翻；一八五五年秋在奧基喬比湖東北岸的泰勒溪一帶開戰議時，他主張回應美軍的增兵，十二月二十日率四十人突擊哈蘇夫中尉的運輸隊，此後兩年以游擊牽制美軍，最後在一八五八年接受西遷並抵達印第安領域。奇普科在戰議上反對開戰，他率領的穆斯科吉人隊伍最終未降；薩姆·瓊斯帶領密克蘇基人小隊退入大沼澤地；奧斯森·圖斯滕吉則率隊攻擊佛丹諾堡外的伐木巡邏，並在一八五六年六月和平河上游的戰鬥中陣亡。聯邦方面，陸軍部長傑佛遜·戴維斯在一八五四年推動以禁運、售地與增兵迫使遷徙的方案；佛州州長詹姆斯·布魯姆組織志願兵與民兵；傑西·卡特以「無軍階特別代理」身分率領州部隊；准將威廉·哈尼在一八五六年九月重整戰線，改以橫貫佛州的堡壘線封鎖沼澤；上校古斯塔夫斯·盧米斯接任後以金屬「鱷魚艇」深入大柏樹沼澤搜尋；一八五七年聯邦第五步兵團被調往堪薩斯；陸軍上尉阿布納·達布爾迪則指出士兵多為新近移民、缺乏林地生存本領，是搜捕成效不彰的主因。
peopleEn: On the Seminole side Billy Bowlegs was the best known leader of the Third Seminole War. In 1852 the removal agent Luther Blake took him to Washington, where President Millard Fillmore gave him a silver medal; he and three other chiefs signed an agreement to move west and repudiated it as soon as they were back in Florida. At the war council held near Taylor Creek on the north-east shore of Lake Okeechobee in the autumn of 1855 he pressed for a reply to the arrival of United States troops, and on 20 December he led forty men into the attack on Lieutenant Hartsuff's wagon convoy; for two more years he tied the Americans down with raids, and in 1858 he finally accepted removal and reached Indian Territory. Chipco argued against war at that council, and the Muscogee-speaking band he led never surrendered; Sam Jones took a small Miccosukee group deep into the Everglades; Oscen Tustenuggee led the attack on the wood-cutting patrol outside Fort Denaud and was killed in the fight on the Peace River in June 1856. On the federal side Secretary of War Jefferson Davis drove the programme of 1854 that combined trade embargo, land sales and added troops to force removal; Governor James Broome organised volunteers and militia; Carter led the state troops as a 'special agent without military rank'; Brigadier General William S. Harney reorganised the theatre in September 1856 into a line of forts across Florida to seal the swamps; Colonel Gustavus Loomis took over and searched the Big Cypress with metal 'alligator boats'; the 5th Infantry was transferred to Kansas in 1857; and Captain Abner Doubleday observed that the enlistees were mostly recent immigrants without woodcraft, which was why the searches achieved so little.
kits: 卡面這件法國一八四〇年雷管步槍是這場戰役的技術底色：底火取代火燧之後，佛州沼澤地常年的濕氣與雨霧不再使槍械失靈，射程拉長，射手可以在數百米外單發精射，交火距離因此被槍械性能重新定義。聯軍步兵主要使用一八四二年式與一八五五年式雷管步槍、騎槍與一八五五年式步槍騎槍，另有四二年式與五五年式手槍，第四砲兵團配備六磅野砲與榴彈砲。真正把隊伍帶進沼澤的是工具而不是槍：早於此役已經造好的金屬「鱷魚艇」長約三十英尺、兩端尖削、吃水只有二至三英尺，可載十六人，專用於進入大柏樹沼澤與大沼澤地中的孤島與高地。運輸方面，軍用馬車與騾隊是塞米諾爾人最想攻擊的目標：一八五五年十二月二十日，四十名塞米諾爾人正是殺死騾子、搶走並燒毀哈蘇夫中尉的兩輛馬車，令這支小隊當場喪失移動能力。塞米諾爾人自己的火器多為商售火槍改裝雷管以及獵槍，同樣是前膛單發、每發都要中途中裝填，另備弓矢、長矛、砍刀與戰棒。州民兵裝備多由民間捐款籌措，口徑與制式不一，火藥在雨季容易受潮，遇上連日雨勢時即威力大減。
kitsEn: The percussion rifle on this card, a French model of 1840, is the technical background of this campaign. Once percussion replaced the flint, the damp and the fog that hang over the Florida swamps no longer put a weapon out of action; the range grew and a shooter could place single aimed shots at several hundred metres, so the range at which fights were decided was set by the weapon rather than by the terrain. The American infantry used the 1842 and 1855 percussion rifles, carbines and the 1855 rifle-musket, with the 1842 and 1855 pistols, and the 4th Artillery carried six-pounder field guns and howitzers. What actually carried troops into the swamp was equipment rather than firearms: the metal 'alligator boats', built before the war specifically for the Big Cypress and the Everglades, were about thirty feet long, pointed at both ends, drew two to three feet of water and could carry sixteen men, and were used to reach islands and dry ground inside the marshes. On the logistics side, army wagons and mule teams were what the Seminoles most wanted to hit: on 20 December 1855 the forty Seminoles killed the mules and looted and burned Lieutenant Hartsuff's two wagons, and the patrol lost its mobility on the spot. The Seminole firearms were mostly trade muskets converted to percussion and hunting guns, equally single-shot muzzleloaders that had to be reloaded between every shot, and they also carried bows and arrows, lances, knives and war clubs. The state militia was armed largely with private donations, in mixed calibres and no common standard, and its powder easily went damp in the wet season, which took much of the edge off the weapon whenever the rains came.
tactics: 塞米諾爾人延續第二次戰爭的游擊辦法：不做會戰，只挑目標明確的小隊下手。一八五五年秋在泰勒溪的戰議決定以突擊回應增兵與遷徙壓力；十二月二十日四十人攻擊哈蘇夫中尉的十人馬車隊，殺傷四人之後破壞騾子與馬車，令美軍的糧秣與信件斷鏈；一八五六年初又襲擊佛丹諾堡外的伐木巡邏，一支六人巡邏折損五人；四月在鮑萊格斯鎮外打了六個鐘頭，擊斃四名正規軍之後主動撤離，不作追擊，也不佔據地形。聯軍的戰術主線是封鎖加搜索：一八五六年九月哈尼准將沿佛州橫貫全境布置一列堡壘，把塞米諾爾人限制在大柏樹沼澤與大沼澤地，指望雨季過後他們離開淹水的藏身地去整地種植時予以截獲；盧米斯接手後以金屬鱷魚艇搜索沼澤中的小島；民兵巡邏多避開林莽專走開闊地，馬匹好走，卻讓塞米諾爾人遠遠就看見來人；州部隊因火藥受潮，一遇雨勢即被迫退卻。最後奏效的仍是搜索並摧毀村落與玉米田的消耗辦法：摧毀供給，等於逼出投降。
tacticsEn: The Seminoles carried the guerrilla methods of the Second War forward: no set-piece battle, only attacks on small, clearly identified targets. The council at Taylor Creek in the autumn of 1855 decided to answer the pressure of reinforcements and removal with raids. On 20 December forty men hit Lieutenant Hartsuff's wagon convoy of ten men, killed several of them and then destroyed the mules and the wagons, cutting the mail and the food supply. Early in 1856 they struck the wood-cutting patrol outside Fort Denaud, where a patrol of six lost five men; in April they fought for six hours outside Bowlegs Town, killed four regulars and then withdrew on their own terms, neither pursuing nor holding the ground. The American line of method was blockade plus search. In September 1856 Harney laid a chain of forts right across Florida to confine the Seminoles to the Big Cypress and the Everglades, in the expectation that when the wet season passed and they left the flooded refuges to plant their crops they could be caught in the open. Loomis, who followed, searched the islands of the swamp with the metal alligator boats. Militia patrols avoided the woods and rode the open country, which suited the horses but let the Seminoles see them coming from a long way off, and state troops were forced to break off whenever rain spoiled their powder. What finally worked was the old search-and-destroy routine applied to villages and cornfields: destroy the supply and surrender becomes the only option left.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下。第二次塞米諾爾戰爭到一八四二年結束時，共約三千六百一十二人遷往印第安領域，佛州只餘三百五十至五百人；一八四七年陸軍上尉斯普拉吉清點為一百二十名戰士，其中鮑萊格斯部七十人、薩姆·瓊斯部密克蘇基人三十人、奇普科部穆斯科吉人十二人，另有尤奇四人、喬克托四人，另有婦女一百人、兒童一百四十人。戰前佛州民兵在邊界上的搜捕只抓到一名男子、數名婦女與一百四十頭豬，整個行動花費州府四萬美元。一八五一年遷徙使者的條件是每名成年男子八百美元、每名婦女與兒童四百五十美元，到一八五二年七月只說服十六人西遷。一八五五年底佛州半島上的聯邦軍已超過七百人；州方在遭襲後組織的志願兵中，兩個步兵連與三個騎兵連約二百六十人被聯邦收編，另有約四百人由州政府自領，卡特抽出一半人耕種，實際可用於巡邏的只剩二百人。一八五五年十二月二十日，四十名塞米諾爾人對付十名美軍，斃傷四人，七人退回邁爾斯堡，其中四人受傷。一八五六年四月鮑萊格斯鎮一役歷時六小時，聯軍死四傷三；六月十四日梅德堡外的七名騎兵民兵遭襲，卡爾頓中尉、洛特·惠登與威廉·帕克三人陣亡、兩人受傷；十六日福瑞瑟堡民兵在和平河上游交戰，民兵死二傷三，宣稱擊斃二十名塞米諾爾人，塞米諾爾方面只承認四人陣亡、兩人受傷。一八五七年十個民兵連被聯邦收編，到九月接近八百人。結算的價碼是每名戰士五百美元、首領加碼、每名婦女一百美元；鮑萊格斯一系另記為首領得一萬美元、其餘首領各一千美元。一八五八年三月十五日鮑萊格斯與阿辛瓦爾兩隊接受，五月四日共一百六十三人被運上新奧良的船，五月八日盧米斯上校宣布戰爭結束。官方當時估計佛州僅餘百人左右，同年十二月再招募兩批共七十五人，一八五九年二月十五日運走。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. When the Second Seminole War ended in 1842 about three thousand six hundred and twelve people had been moved to Indian Territory and only three hundred and fifty to five hundred were left in Florida. In 1847 the Army captain Sprague counted one hundred and twenty warriors, seventy in Bowlegs' band, thirty Miccosukees in Sam Jones' band and twelve Muscogees in Chipco's band, with four Yuchi and four Choctaw besides, together with about one hundred women and one hundred and forty children. Before the war the Florida militia caught only one man and a few women along the boundary and one hundred and forty hogs, and the whole operation cost the state forty thousand dollars. In 1851 the removal agent was funded to pay eight hundred dollars for every adult male and four hundred and fifty for every woman and child, and by July 1852 he had persuaded only sixteen people to go west. By the end of 1855 more than seven hundred regulars were on the Florida peninsula; of the volunteers raised after the raid, two infantry companies and three mounted companies of about two hundred and sixty men were taken over by the federal government, another four hundred remained under state control, and Carter could find only two hundred fit for patrol because half were set to growing crops. On 20 December 1855 forty Seminoles fought ten Americans, killing several; seven men, four of them wounded, made it back to Fort Myers. At Bowlegs Town in April 1856 the fight lasted six hours and the Americans lost four killed and three wounded. On 14 June the seven mounted militiamen sent out from Fort Meade were attacked and Alderman Carlton, Lott Whidden and William Parker were killed with two more wounded; on the 16th the Fort Fraser militia met the Seminoles on the Peace River, losing two killed and three wounded while claiming twenty Seminole dead, an account the Seminoles themselves put at four dead and two wounded. In 1857 ten militia companies were taken into federal service and by September numbered close to eight hundred men. The settlement offered five hundred dollars a warrior, more for the chiefs, and a hundred dollars a woman; the Bowlegs account gives ten thousand dollars to the chief himself and a thousand to each subchief. On 15 March 1858 Bowlegs and Assinwar accepted, on 4 May one hundred and sixty-three people were put aboard a ship for New Orleans, and on 8 May Colonel Loomis declared the war over. Official estimates put the number still in Florida at about a hundred, and in December two more bands of seventy-five in all were recruited and shipped out on 15 February 1859.
cause: 第三次塞米諾爾戰爭不是突然爆發的，而是第二次戰爭結束後十三年的遷徙僵局最終被打破。一八四二年停戰時，殘餘塞米諾爾人被安置在佛州西南部一塊非正式保留地，同年通過的《武裝占領法》鼓勵移民在坦帕以南拓殖，一八四五年總統波爾克又在保留地周圍劃出二十英里寬的緩衝帶禁止落户，保留地的界線被越來越緊地擠壓。佛州當局不斷要求聯邦把人全部送走：一八五一年內政部任命盧瑟·布萊克執行遷徙，他帶鮑萊格斯等首領赴華盛頓，總統費爾莫爾頒章並說服四人簽下遷徙協議，首領返程即翻供；布萊克一八五三年被撤換，遷徙使者的談判屢屢無功。一八五四年八月，陸軍部長傑佛遜·戴維斯啟動一套把塞米諾爾人逼入最後決戰的方案：切斷貿易、測量並出售佛州南部土地給移民、加派軍隊護衛新居民，並明言若不肯遷走就用武力。聯邦同時設立保留地，在鮑萊格斯的地界上修築堡壘，工兵沿途毀掉庄稼，後世史家認為這是刻意的挑釁。外部壓力累積到一八五五年秋，塞米諾爾人在奧基喬比湖東北岸的泰勒溪一帶集會，戰士老虎主張動武、奇普科反對，結果十二月的伏擊把整件事變成了公開戰爭。
causeEn: The Third Seminole War did not break out suddenly; it came out of a thirteen-year stalemate over removal that followed the end of the Second War. When the fighting stopped in 1842 the remaining Seminoles were left on an informal reservation in south-western Florida; the Armed Occupation Act passed in the same year encouraged settlers to move south of Tampa, and in 1845 President Polk drew a buffer twenty miles wide around the reservation in which no one could take title, so the reservation was squeezed from every side. The state authorities in Florida kept pressing the federal government to move the last people out. In 1851 the Department of the Interior appointed Luther Blake to carry out removal; he took Bowlegs and other chiefs to Washington, where President Fillmore presented a medal and persuaded four of them to sign an agreement to move west, and they repudiated it on the way home. Blake was removed in 1853 and the talks with the removal agent went nowhere. In August 1854 Secretary of War Jefferson Davis set in motion a plan to force the Seminoles into a final conflict: a trade embargo, the survey and sale of land in southern Florida to immigrants, more troops to protect the new settlers, and the plain statement that force would be used if the Seminoles would not go. At the same time the government set up a reservation and built forts inside Bowlegs' territory, and the engineer parties destroyed crops on the way; later historians have read those acts as deliberate provocation. The pressure came to a head in the autumn of 1855, when the Seminoles met near Taylor Creek on the north-east shore of Lake Okeechobee. The warrior Tiger argued for war and Chipco against it, and the December ambush turned the whole business into an open war.
impact: 這場戰爭留下的第一項影響是佛州南部的土地版圖。一八五八年之後，絕大多數塞米諾爾人遷往印第安領域，塞米諾爾族在奧克拉荷馬州建立了獨立的保留地與行政機關；留在佛州的人退入奧基喬比湖周邊與大沼澤地的高地小塊地帶，以數百人的規模延續了獨立的聚落，佛羅里達塞米諾爾族至今主張自己是唯一從未與美國政府簽過和平條約的部族。第二項影響是聯邦與州的權責分配：聯邦軍隊長期駐紮，聯邦卻不願為佛州的戰爭撥款，軍費主要由州府與民間捐款負擔，州民兵裝備雜亂、指揮系統重疊，戰後州內對聯邦的不信任一路累積到一八六〇年的選舉與分裂危機。第三項是軍事的教訓：後膛雷管槍在雨霧中可靠、射程更遠，卻抵擋不住對後勤與馬車隊的定點襲擊；真正解決問題的是堡壘線、沼澤小艇、搜索摧毀村落的消耗戰，最後再加上一筆現金。第四項是對後來政策的影響：聯邦以金錢買遷徙、以交易代替戰爭的做法，成為十九世紀末美國對待原住民部族的常態。一八六八年佛州憲法曾給塞米諾爾人在州議會各留一席，兩席從未有人就任，一八八五年修憲時被廢除。
impactEn: The first effect of the war was on the map of south Florida. After 1858 the great majority of the Seminoles were moved to Indian Territory, where the Seminole Nation built its own reservation and agency in what is now Oklahoma; those who stayed in Florida withdrew to the high ground around Lake Okeechobee and in the Everglades and carried on as small independent settlements of several hundred people. The Seminole Tribe of Florida still holds that it is the only tribe never to have signed a peace treaty with the United States government. The second effect was on the division of authority between the federal government and the state. Federal troops were stationed in Florida for years while Congress declined to pay for a war it considered the state's own business; the cost fell on the state treasury and on private donations, the militia was armed in mixed calibres, and the two chains of command overlapped. The distrust of the federal government that the war produced fed straight into the elections of 1860 and the secession crisis. The third effect was a military lesson: the percussion rifle fired reliably in the wet and reached further, but it could not stop an ambush aimed at the baggage and the wagon teams. What solved the problem was the line of forts, the boats that could work the swamps, the search-and-destroy campaign against the villages, and finally a sum of money. The fourth effect ran into later policy: the federal practice of buying removal, of paying for departure instead of winning a war, became the normal form of United States dealings with Native nations in the late nineteenth century. The 1868 Florida constitution gave the Seminoles one seat each in the state house and senate, a provision that was never filled and was struck out when the constitution was replaced in 1885.
result: 過程是一條緩慢下坡的曲線。一八五五年十二月二十日哈蘇夫中尉的馬車隊被襲，是這場戰爭的第一聲槍；一八五六年上半年接連是伐木巡邏遭伏、鮑萊格斯鎮外的六小時交鋒、和平河上游的民兵反擊，聯軍以兵力和補給換來的是一次次小勝利，代價卻是持續的傷亡與日益惡化的財政。一八五六年九月哈尼准將接手，把戰線拉成一條橫貫佛州的堡壘鏈，試圖用雨季困死沼澤中的游擊隊；一八五七年春他與第五步兵團調往堪薩斯，戰區只剩第四砲兵團十個連，後來只剩四個連，盧米斯上校靠金屬鱷魚艇在沼澤裡搜出的人數遠多於正規軍。轉折點不在戰場而在談判：一八五八年一月，印第安領域派來代表勸說鮑萊格斯，開出每名戰士五百美元、首領加碼、每名婦女一百美元的價碼，三月十五日鮑萊格斯與阿辛瓦爾兩支隊伍接受，五月四日一百六十三人上船赴新奧良，五月八日盧米斯上校宣布戰爭結束。戰果可以這樣結算：聯邦以軍費換到了一次遷移，塞米諾爾人保住數百人存續的代價是分成數批被拆散西送，仍拒絕遷徙的數支小隊伍繼續在奧基喬比湖與大沼澤地以小規模游擊存在。就兵器而言，雷管步槍在這條線上只是其中一環：它讓佛州雨季的射程與精度不再是障礙，卻沒有、也不可能解決騾子、馬車、堡壘線與現金所決定的問題。
resultEn: The course of the thing was a long, slow downward slope. The ambush of Lieutenant Hartsuff's wagon convoy on 20 December 1855 was the first shot of the war. Through the first half of 1856 came the ambush of the wood-cutting patrol, the six hours of fighting outside Bowlegs Town and the militia counter-stroke on the Peace River; the Americans bought these small successes with men and supplies, and paid for them with a running tally of casualties and a steadily worsening treasury. Brigadier General Harney took over in September 1856 and drew the front into a chain of forts right across Florida, hoping to starve the guerrillas out in the flooded swamps. When he and the 5th Infantry were sent to Kansas in the spring of 1857 the theatre was left with ten companies of the 4th Artillery, later only four, and Colonel Loomis took far more people out of the marshes with metal alligator boats than the regulars ever managed to catch. The turning point was not on the battlefield but at the negotiating table. In January 1858 a delegation from Indian Territory came to argue with Bowlegs and the offer was five hundred dollars a warrior, more for the chiefs and a hundred dollars a woman; on 15 March Bowlegs and Assinwar accepted, on 4 May one hundred and sixty-three people boarded the ship for New Orleans, and on 8 May Colonel Loomis declared the war over. The account can be settled this way: the United States bought a removal with military money, and the Seminoles kept a few hundred people alive at the price of being shipped west in broken-up batches, while the bands that still refused to go on making a living as small bands of raiders around Lake Okeechobee and the Everglades. As for the weapon, the percussion rifle was one link in that chain: it removed the range and the wet as obstacles to shooting, but it could not and did not settle the questions settled by the mules, the wagons, the line of forts and the cash.
